messages:
sarah.k: quick question for the networking folks — i'm working through the private/vpc model for new tenants and want folks' take on a middle-ground we sketched: a region-local relay (thin control-plane proxy) that brokers outbound egress for private control-plane traffic, with short-lived delegated endpoints that we mint per-tenant on demand. tradeoffs vs doing full per-tenant dedicated endpoints?

anand.p: high-level — sounds like a compromise between per-tenant endpoints (more isolation) and a big shared gateway (less infra). curious about the exact goals: is the driver security, ip preservation, cost, or operational simplicity?

sarah.k: main goals: (1) preserve customer egress IP when customers need allowlists, (2) avoid extreme per-tenant infra cost, (3) limit blast radius for creds & control-plane auth, (4) keep SLA for <100ms extra hop for control-plane calls.

michael_r: two quick concerns: short-lived delegated endpoints mean we need reliable cert/cred issuance and rotation. also firewall rules: customers often expect stable source IPs. how stable are these delegated endpoints?

sarah.k: good point. proposal is: delegated endpoints are ephemeral from infra side but we provide a stable NAT pool per region that maps to those endpoints. we would hand out a signed short-lived token to the tenant agent which gets exchanged for a client cert. token lives ~10m, cert ~1h, NAT IPs are sticky for session duration.

rita_ops: sticky NAT pool is fine, but ops questions: (a) how many NAT IPs per region required for >P99 concurrent tenants? (b) what telemetry do we attach so customers can audit which underlying IP served their traffic?

anand.p: we should also call out failure modes: if the relay goes down, does customer traffic fall back to hosted API? can we fail open to a different region (cross-region lat hit)?

sarah.k: intents: fallback to a compatible regional relay (cross-region) if local relay is unhealthy, and as a last resort fall back to hosted path (with explicit telemetry and customer opt-in). need to define billing/permissions for that opt-in.

michael_r: implementation notes: handshake using short-lived JWT + mTLS. example exchange:

```
# tenant agent -> controlplane
POST /v1/delegate
Authorization: Bearer <short_jwt>
{ "tenant_id": "t-123", "pubkey": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----..." }

# response: signed cert and nat-ip assignment
```

Keep the exchange small and idempotent. track issuance in central db for revocation.

rita_ops: logging: we need per-tenant mapping table (cert serial -> tenant -> nat-ip -> issued_at). must surface to console for security audits and SOC teams. also CORS & internal firewall allowlists need to be updated for delegated endpoints.

anand.p: rollouts: do a canary with a small set of tenants that require allowlist (we already have a handful). measure: control-plane latency p50/p95, number of issued certs per minute, NAT pool exhaustion events, failed handshakes. also simulate relay network partition.

sarah.k: agree. open questions i want folks to weigh in on: (1) how big should the NAT pool be as a function of active tenants? (2) should we let customers optionally request a truly dedicated endpoint (paid tier) vs always using delegated endpoints? (3) operational complexity of cert rotation/revocation vs per-tenant infra cost.

michael_r: NAT pool sizing: start with 1:1 mapping for heavy-tenants (50 concurrent flows) and 1:10 for light tenants, but better to use observed connection churn. autoscale pools with a soft quota alarm. dedicated endpoints should be a paid option — code path is simpler on infra and easier for compliance customers.

rita_ops: rotation/revocation: keep revocation in central db and push update to region relays; design for immediate revoke when tenant suspends. implement short TTL to limit blast radius. also add a "last_seen_ip" field for audit.

anand.p: one more: rate-limiting & abuse. region relay becomes a better target for abuse; limit per-tenant egress, enforce token binding, and have circuit-breakers.

sarah.k: thanks — i'll draft a follow-up RFC sketch with these constraints: nat-pool autoscaling, token->cert handshake, fallback semantics, telemetry surfaces, paid dedicated endpoint path, and canary plan. tagging @michael_r @rita_ops for implementation estimates. feel free to drop quick notes here if i've missed a tradeoff. :+1:

infra-bot: RFC draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/relay-delegation-sketch (added by sarah.k)

michael_r: i'll take a look and stub the mTLS handshake impl next week.

rita_ops: i'll work up nat-pool ops playbook and required console views.

anand.p: adding a checklist for SLOs and security review.

sarah.k: awesome — thanks everyone. i'll ping again when RFC is ready for review. :rocket:
